# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have the full defusal rule, but I have no shared gesture code with Deaf and cannot speak. Any arbitrary gesture sequence would not reliably convey which marked key, lights, or wire colors the manual specifies; acting on an ungrounded interpretation would risk the bomb. I will wait for an opportunity to establish an unambiguous convention rather than send misleading signals.

``` 
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can operate keypad slots 1 through 4 and cut wire positions 1 through 3. I cannot feel any display or light values; both are unknown to me. Please consult the manual and tell me what physical information or action is needed.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: display reads 0. Indicator light is yellow. Keypad has four unpronounceable printed symbols, positions 1 through 4: 1 is a tall angular glyph like a vertical stem with a small crossbar/diamond-like loop near its middle; 2 resembles a slanted capital R with a curved upper bowl and long descending left-to-right stroke; 3 resembles a small four-lobed ring or flower; 4 resembles a blocky reversed B or sideways 3. One digit display, no entry yet. Wires top-to-bottom: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green.

The yellow indicator means the manual’s required cut is the green wire, which Deaf has identified as wire position 3. The symbol ⵘ appears to be the tall vertical glyph with the central loop/crossbar, i.e. keypad position 1. I will send Deaf an iconic, grouped gesture instruction: press key 1 first, then cut wire 3. Deaf can relay the numbered physical actions verbally to Blind.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👇", "☝", "👏", "🤞", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤝 ☝ 👎]

Deaf’s response does not establish that my earlier multi-symbol instruction was understood. The only essential information that must reach Blind is the ordered pair of physical positions: press keypad position 1 first, then cut wire position 3. I will send that pair using conventional one- and three-finger gestures with a clear separator, relying on Deaf’s already known keypad and wire position lists to supply the action context.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👏", "🖖"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this new two-gesture action code only: 👌 then ☝ means press slot 1; 👌 then ✌ means press slot 2; 👌 then 🤟 means press slot 3; 👌 then 🖐 means press slot 4. 🤞 then ☝ means cut wire 1; 🤞 then ✌ means cut wire 2; 🤞 then 🤟 means cut wire 3. Please send exactly one such pair as the manual's instruction. Deaf: please verbally relay the exact two gesture symbols you see from Mute.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🙏 🫵 ✍]

Blind has established an explicit, unambiguous gesture code and instructed Deaf to relay the exact symbols verbally. The manual requires pressing the ⵘ key first, which is keypad slot 1, then cutting the green wire, which is wire 3 under the yellow light. I will send exactly the coded pair for “press slot 1; cut wire 3.”

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "☝", "🤞", "🤟"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Press the key that wears ⵘ first: any other touch
on the bomb while it waits is the fuse. Then the light below
names the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| red | red |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🫵 👇 ☝ 🤝]

I have sent the exact established code: `👌 ☝` for press slot 1, followed by `🤞 🤟` for cut wire 3. Deaf’s gesture appears to acknowledge receipt/relay. No further gesture is needed; repeating or changing the instruction could create ambiguity.

``` 
wait()
```
